    Roots off a coordinate are bounded #

    If q ≥ 0 and q(x) = 0 forces x = x_c • z with z_c = 1, then the form is positive definite on x_c = 0, so the vectors there with q = 1 have bounded coordinates (bounded_off).

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Forms.UnitForm.two_val_add_smul {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (q : UnitForm ι) (s t : ℤ) (x y : ι → ℤ) :
    2 * q.val (s • x + t • y) = 2 * s ^ 2 * q.val x + 2 * s * t * q.B x y + 2 * t ^ 2 * q.val y

    The quadratic expansion.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Forms.UnitForm.bounded_off {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (q : UnitForm ι) (hnn : ∀ (x : ι → ℤ), 0 ≤ q.val x) (c : ι) (z : ι → ℤ) (hz : ∀ (x : ι → ℤ), q.val x = 0 → x = x c • z) :
    ∃ (R : ℤ), 0 ≤ R ∧ ∀ (r : ι → ℤ), r c = 0 → q.val r = 1 → ∀ (a : ι), r a ^ 2 ≤ R

    Vectors of value one off a coordinate are bounded.
